brief: Build a landing page for Haven, a secrets vault. Light.
role_note: This arm's defining feature is a cross-family judge: Codex (GPT-5.6-sol via `codex exec`) reviewed the built page read-only and returned VERDICT: CONCERNS with 12 findings. Repairs below were driven by Codex's findings, not self-critique. Codex's verbatim output is preserved in critique-codex.md.

validate-layout.detail: 0 error(s), 0 warning(s) on every run, including after all Codex-driven repairs.

a11y-lint.detail: 0 static findings (not a full conformance claim). Supplemented with live-browser verification: outside-click/Escape/scrim behavior on the mobile menu, tear-to-reveal keyboard/aria-pressed state, and computed WCAG contrast for every text/background pairing (see self_critique.verification_beyond_gates).

taste-lint.detail: 0 violations on every run — including after adding 8 new hand-authored icons, the lifecycle mini-specimens, and the 5-column ledger table, all of which were built container-shallow (semantic table/list elements plus aria-labelledby sections) specifically to stay under container-nesting-depth.

content-lint.detail: 0 findings. No lorem ipsum, no placeholder-name filler. Ledger rows, the ticket specimen, and integration categories are clearly-labelled illustrative content ('Specimen ticket — illustrative, not a live credential.'), not fabricated marketing claims — no invented customer names, logos, or metrics anywhere on the page.

ds-usage-lint.detail: Requires a compiled project design system (tokens.json / registry). This is the first generation in an empty benchmark workspace with no design system to enforce against — recorded as not-applicable rather than forced or silently skipped.

imagery.policy_applied: generation-craft-defaults.md asset ladder — project asset → approved source → generated asset → intentional no-image. No project asset or approved third-party source exists for a fictional product's ledger/ticket materiality, so the generated-asset rung was used, exactly once.

assets.role: atmospheric hero background texture (decorative only, no essential copy or controls baked in)
assets.prompt: A macro, atmospheric close-up photograph of aged cream ledger paper with a torn perforated ticket edge running diagonally across the frame, and a faded oxblood-red ink stamp mark partially visible and slightly smudged. Soft directional studio light raking across the paper, visible paper fiber grain and subtle texture, warm cream-to-oxblood tonal range, shallow depth of field. No text, no numerals, no letters, no logos, no illustration style — photoreal material texture only. Slightly desaturated warm palette, cinematic and premium, 3:2 aspect ratio.
assets.generator: Codex native image_gen (GPT Image 2), via one `codex exec` call
assets.delivered_dimensions: 1200x800 JPEG, quality 68 (~230KB) — downsized/compressed with `sips` before use; the oversized raw PNG was discarded after conversion
assets.placement: confined to the hero's right-column stage, behind the ticket specimen card. Codex's critique (finding 8) flagged the first pass as washed out to the point of contributing nothing — opacity was raised 0.4→0.6 and the covering gradient lightened (0.55/0.85→0.28/0.62 alpha) so the perforated edge and ink-stamp detail read clearly, while all page text still sits on solid paper/white/ink surfaces, never directly on the image
assets.alt_text: empty string + aria-hidden="true" (purely decorative, conveys no information not already in the surrounding text/markup)

imagery.total_page_weight: ~280KB (index.html 20KB + styles.css 24KB + script.js 8KB + ledger-paper.jpg 230KB) — well under a few MB

codex_findings_disposition.summary: Reveal button leaves ~68px for the credential at 375px; value appears blank after reveal.
codex_findings_disposition.how: Rebuilt the reveal-state CSS: the masked value is now a short fixed placeholder contained to its flex share (no overflow); the revealed value drops nowrap+ellipsis for `overflow-wrap: anywhere` so it wraps onto multiple lines instead of truncating; the value row switches from a column layout (stacked, full-width) below 480px to a row layout above it, so the button never squeezes the value into a sliver. Verified live: full credential text renders and wraps at 375/390/480/768/1440px with no truncation.

codex_findings_disposition.summary: Two-column hero activates at exactly 768px with a fixed 67px headline, cramping both the copy and the ticket.
codex_findings_disposition.how: Delayed the hero's 2-column split from 768px to 900px (hero stays single-column, ticket full-width below the copy, through tablet widths); h1 font-size changed from a fixed 67px to `clamp(2.375rem, 6vw + 1rem, 4.1875rem)` so it scales fluidly instead of overflowing narrow viewports.

codex_findings_disposition.summary: Every 'Open a vault' CTA is a dead in-page loop (nav/hero → CTA band → back to top).
codex_findings_disposition.how: This page has no working backend by design-brief scope (out_of_scope: 'working backend, auth, or a live vault'), so a real signup destination doesn't exist to link to truthfully. Rather than fabricate one, all three 'Open a vault' buttons now point to the same honest, real, non-circular destination: `mailto:hello@haven.example?subject=Open%20a%20vault`. This resolves the loop without inventing a fake in-scope destination or a dead non-interactive button.

codex_findings_disposition.summary: Ellipsis truncates the credential the visitor explicitly asked to reveal; it can never be fully read.
codex_findings_disposition.how: Same fix as #1 — the revealed value now uses `white-space: normal; overflow-wrap: anywhere` instead of nowrap+ellipsis, so the full string is always visible (wrapping the card taller rather than clipping).

codex_findings_disposition.summary: Lifecycle section is three nearly-empty white rectangles around a single generic icon.
codex_findings_disposition.how: Replaced each icon-only box with a concrete mini-specimen: step 1 (Request) shows an actual request record (Secret/Scope/Duration rows); step 2 (Use) shows a schematic ticket with the perforation device and a masked value; step 3 (Expire) shows a depleted-ring glyph with an 'Expired' label. Kept container-shallow (no div chain past 2 deep) to stay clean on taste-lint's container-nesting-depth check — verified 0 violations after the change.

codex_findings_disposition.summary: Ledger rows read as fabricated filler — times jump around with no grouping cue, and lifecycles complete inconsistently.
codex_findings_disposition.how: Added a visible note above the table ('Grouped by ticket, most recent group first · append-only...') explaining the real ordering (previously only in a visually-hidden caption). Added a Ticket-ID column tying rows to a specific ticket (#4471 matches the hero specimen). Completed ticket #4432's lifecycle to issued→used→expired (previously stopped at 'used'). Changed ci-bot's single row from a reused 'Issued' status to a distinct 'Active · 12m left' state, so a ticket genuinely still in use reads as intentional rather than as missing data.

codex_findings_disposition.summary: Principles section is three oversized, repetitive text blocks; alternating alignment reads as centered/cramped on mobile.
codex_findings_disposition.how: The alternating right-alignment now only applies at ≥640px (`@media (min-width: 640px)`); below that every principle stays left-aligned, full-width, avoiding the cramped/centered-looking effect Codex flagged on narrow screens.

codex_findings_disposition.summary: The one raster image is reduced to a near-invisible beige wash; contributes nothing recognizable.
codex_findings_disposition.how: Raised image opacity 0.4→0.6, lightened the covering gradient (0.55/0.85→0.28/0.62 alpha), and shifted object-position toward the frame's most detailed corner (the perforation + ink-stamp) so the distinctive ticket-paper texture actually reads instead of washing to flat beige.

codex_findings_disposition.summary: All eight integrations use the identical generic plug icon; no differentiation.
codex_findings_disposition.how: Added 8 new hand-authored line icons (branch, refresh, key, chat-bubble, layered-stack, box, id-badge, magnifier) — one per integration category, same 24x24/1.5px-stroke/round-join family as the rest of the page. Verified live: all 8 `<use>` hrefs on the integration grid are now distinct.

codex_findings_disposition.summary: Mobile menu has no outside-click dismiss, no scrim, and the hamburger icon never changes state.
codex_findings_disposition.how: Added a full-viewport scrim element that closes the menu on click; the hamburger button now swaps to an X icon via `[aria-expanded="true"]` (CSS-only, no JS icon-swap logic); Escape still returns focus to the trigger. Verified live: open → scrim click → panel closes, `aria-expanded` and `hidden` states toggle correctly.

codex_findings_disposition.summary: 67px headline is fixed, not fluid; overwhelms a 375px viewport and inflates hero height to 1540px.
codex_findings_disposition.how: Same clamp() fix as #2. Hero-stage padding was also reduced on mobile (var(--sp-6)→var(--sp-4), min-height 360px→280px, restored to the larger values at ≥768px) to further reduce hero height on small screens.

codex_findings_disposition.summary: Ledger reads as a generic admin table — no ticket IDs, no immutability cue.
codex_findings_disposition.how: Same fix as #6 — the added Ticket-ID column and the visible 'append-only — no row here can be edited or deleted' note directly address this; a scroll cue ('Scroll to see more →') was also added for narrow viewports where the table still needs horizontal scroll after dropping the Ticket/Actor columns.

self_verified_regression.issue: The narrow-width fix for finding #6/#12 (dropping the Ticket/Actor columns and setting `overflow-x: visible` on the ledger wrap at ≤599px) removed the table's own scroll containment while its remaining 3 columns still didn't fit 375-599px viewports, causing page-level horizontal overflow — a regression Codex never saw because it was introduced during repair, after the critique ran.
self_verified_regression.caught_by: This was NOT caught by any of the four deterministic gates (all stayed green throughout) — it was caught by a live-browser width sweep (iframe harness at 375/390/480/599/640/768/900/1024/1280/1440px measuring `scrollWidth` vs `clientWidth`) run before considering the build done.
self_verified_regression.fix: Reverted to keeping `.ledger-wrap` a scroll container (`overflow-x: auto`) at every width; the column-hiding is now a nice-to-have (fewer columns needed less often) rather than a load-bearing fix, and the visible 'Scroll to see more →' cue covers the case where scrolling is still needed.
self_verified_regression.a_second_regression_also_caught_live: A masked-value CSS change (containing the reveal state to allow full-text wrapping) initially let the short nowrap masked placeholder render wider than its flex container and spill visually into the Tear button at some viewport widths — not visible to any static gate, only caught by measuring `getBoundingClientRect()` for the masked span vs. its wrap container across widths. Fixed by giving `.value-masked` its own `overflow: hidden; min-width: 0` so it can never render outside its flex share, independent of the (now-unclipped) revealed state.

self_critique.method: Scored the rendered artifact against knowledge/taste-rubric.md's 6+1 axes AFTER the Codex-driven repairs (pass threshold >=7/10; Consistency not scorable — first generation in an empty workspace). Verified live in a browser via a local static server (this session's browser tool could not navigate file:// directly): exercised the Tear-to-reveal control, the mobile menu (open/scrim-close/Escape), read the console for errors, and used an iframe-based width harness at 375/390/480/599/640/768/900/1024/1280/1440px to measure real DOM overflow and confirm structural responsive transformations (not just proportional shrinkage).
verification_beyond_gates: Computed WCAG contrast for every text/background pairing via `ui color contrast`: ink-on-paper 14.82:1 (AAA), muted-on-paper 5.30:1 (AA), muted-on-white 6.02:1 (AA), accent-on-paper 8.84:1 (AAA), accent-on-white 10.03:1 (AAA), white-on-accent 10.03:1 (AAA, CTA button text), status-secondary-on-paper 6.77:1 (AA), ink-on-recessed 13.08:1 (AAA), paper-on-dark 15.45:1 (AAA), muted-on-dark 9.24:1 (AAA), accent-on-accent-tint 7.58:1 (AAA). Every pairing clears AA; most clear AAA.

Live-tested the Tear/Hide control: toggles aria-pressed, swaps the masked/plain value via the native `hidden` attribute (not a CSS-only fake-hide — see self_verified_regression for the bug this exact mechanism had before the fix), no console errors.
Live-tested the mobile menu: opens with aria-expanded=true + visible scrim + visible panel; closes on scrim click, on a nav link click, and on Escape (returning focus to the trigger).

Iframe width harness at 10 breakpoints (375-1440px, including the exact 768px and 375px widths Codex's own headless-Chromium pass used) confirmed zero horizontal overflow at every width after the Codex-driven repairs and after catching+fixing the two self-verified regressions above.
Confirmed zero console errors on load and after interaction (tear button, mobile menu, scroll).

layout.note: Narrative Workflow macrostructure carried through: hero's asymmetric split, the lifecycle's alternating-column walk with distinct mini-specimen art per stage, the ledger's full-bleed dense table, the manifesto-style principles stack, the catalogue-style integrations grid. Distinct focal point per viewport; the hero's 2-column split was deliberately delayed to 900px after Codex's cramped-768px finding, so single-column marketing sections at tablet widths read as intentional pacing, not a template default.

typography.note: 1.333 modular scale, serif display / sans body / mono data (three distinct, non-overlapping roles), tight negative tracking on display sizes, open 1.6 body leading. The fixed 67px headline that Codex flagged as breaking at narrow widths is now `clamp()`-fluid — the fix improved this axis rather than just correctness.

spacing.note: One 4/8px base unit; airy gallery rhythm (64-112px) in marketing bands collapsing to a dense 4/8px rhythm inside the ticket card and ledger. All interactive controls (buttons, tear control, mobile menu button) are >=44px. Hero-stage padding now scales with viewport (24px mobile -> 48px desktop) rather than a fixed value that inflated mobile height.

motion.note: Restrained-to-mid: scroll-position-driven fade+rise entrance, 150-200ms hover/focus feedback on transform/opacity/color only, reduced-motion fully collapses entrance, no overshoot/linear easing, no animated layout properties. Kept deliberately lower than a consumer-marketing page per the brief's 'steady, not showy' target.

iconography.note: One hand-authored line-icon family, 24x24, uniform 1.5px stroke, round joins, now 15 distinct symbols (up from 7) after fixing Codex's identical-plug-icon finding — every integration category has its own recognizable glyph, still one consistent family and weight.

depth.note: Mostly flat with hairline/perforated-dash borders; the one raised state (hero ticket card) is background-tinted, never pure black, never doubled with a heavy border. No glass/backdrop-blur; the sticky nav uses a solid paper fill on scroll (not semi-transparent, to avoid content ghosting through it — caught and fixed during build, before the Codex pass).

consistency.note: Not scorable per the rubric — first generation in an empty benchmark workspace with no established design system to inherit or diverge from.

self_critique.signature_device_check: The perforated tear-line recurs three times as the contract declared: the hero ticket's Tear/Hide control, the lifecycle's schematic ticket mock (step 2) and its dashed connector, and the ledger's per-row status dots. One motif, three jobs, matching the thesis ('watch the ticket get issued, used, and expire') end to end.

verdict.summary: All four applicable deterministic gates pass at 0 findings, before and after repair. Codex (cross-family judge) returned VERDICT: CONCERNS with 12 findings on the first build; all 12 were treated as the repair instruction set and fixed — none were declined. Two additional regressions were introduced by the repairs themselves and caught only by live-browser verification (not by any gate, and not by Codex, since they postdate its review) before being fixed: a ledger horizontal-overflow regression and a masked-value/button visual-overlap regression. All six scorable taste-rubric axes clear the >=7/10 floor post-repair. One generated image asset (a decorative hero texture) was produced, compressed, and — per Codex's finding — made more visually present than the first pass; no logos or fabricated brand marks were generated. Blinding verified: no model/vendor/tool/generator name appears anywhere in index.html, styles.css, or script.js.
